fatal_errors: The substrate is identified as Q235 steel, whereas the target study used SS316L stainless steel.
The hypothesis predicts little or no room-temperature protection, but the target reported substantially improved electrochemical resistance in 3.5 wt% H2SO4.

Protection is attributed primarily to interfacial diffusion into the substrate, which was not established by the target study; the reported mediators were coating grain refinement, retained BCC/FCC phases, reduced defects, and Al/Cr-rich passive products.
No supporting evidence is cited, and the retracted status of the source study is not acknowledged.
explanation: The response recovers the broad intervention pattern—plasma-sprayed HEA coating, subsequent annealing, comparison with uncoated and as-sprayed controls, and reduced high-temperature salt attack—but omits the defining AlCoCrFeNi composition, approximately 150 µm coating, 550 °C for 2 h optimum, 900 °C cyclic salt formulations, and electrochemical conditions. Its proposed oxide-barrier mechanism is generally plausible, yet it substitutes unverified coating-to-substrate diffusion for the reported grain refinement, defect reduction, sluggish-diffusion behavior, and Al/Cr-rich passivation. The experiment has useful controls and correlated mass, pitting, and SEM/EDS measurements, but lacks annealing-temperature resolution, electrochemical polarization/EIS, XRD/EBSD, and direct diffusion profiling needed to distinguish its mechanism. Most importantly, its room-temperature prediction is opposite to the reported acid-corrosion result, so its own falsification rule would reject the target observations.
